lesson.menu_title: Talking About Data, Metrics and Results
lesson.menu_desc: Present quarterly results the way managers do: numbers, percentages and trends (increase by, drop from ... to, a sharp drop, increased steadily, higher than the target) — for the Q3 results Daniela presents to the US team: online sales up eighteen percent, checkout time down from ninety to forty-five seconds.
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 24 — Talking About Data, Metrics and Results
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Daniela Feitoza | Lesson 24 -- Talking About Data, Metrics and Results
lesson.grammar_point: describing trends (increase / drop + by / from ... to, adjective + noun vs verb + adverb, higher / lower than)

listenings.text: Hi Daniela, it is Sarah, your English coach. On Thursday you are going to present your quarterly results, so here are three tips for talking about numbers. First, the small words are very important. Use by for the difference: sales increased by eighteen percent. Use from and to for the start and the end: the checkout time dropped from ninety seconds to forty-five. Second, be careful with fifteen and fifty. In fifteen, the stress is at the end: fif-teen. In fifty, the stress is at the start: fif-ty. And we say eighteen percent, never eighteen percents. Third, do not read every number on the slide. The directors want a story, not a list. Choose the three most important numbers, say if the change was sharp or steady, and always compare it with your target. Were you higher or lower than the target? That is the first thing they want to know. Good luck on Thursday, Daniela.

Hi Daniela, it is Greg. I have the numbers from the US stores for the third quarter, and they are not great. Online sales increased slightly, by only four percent. Our target was ten percent, so we are below target. The average checkout time did not change much. It is still about eighty seconds. And in August, support tickets increased sharply, by forty percent, because of the bug in the payment page. In September they dropped again, after the patch. Your numbers in Brazil are much better than ours, especially the checkout time. On Thursday, the directors are going to ask you one question: how did your team do it? So please prepare two or three minutes about the new checkout system. Thanks, Daniela. See you on Thursday.

extra_audio.text: First, online sales increased by eighteen percent, and we were above our target. Then, there was a sharp drop in the average checkout time, from ninety seconds to forty-five. After that, support tickets dropped by thirty percent, to seven hundred a month. Next, app users increased steadily, but they were lower than our target. Finally, our goal for the fourth quarter is a steady increase in app users.
